description:
From docs/research/sat-solver.md (branch research/sat-solver, defk-dtw.21). Ash's authorization now goes through the `crux` package, whose `satisfying_scenarios` runs one solve per scenario plus one per literal to minimise it: one authorization is many small solver calls. The anchors are picosat_elixir (NIF over PicoSAT, ~1 us fixed cost per call, runs on a normal scheduler with no size limit: with +S 1 a 1 ms ticker stalled 3,870 ms on one n = 300 random instance) and simple_sat (pure Elixir, no unit propagation, repeats the full search per variable on UNSAT: a first-pass baseline only). The job is real, the data fits defk, and the yield story is strong.

Kernel: a bounded CDCL solver in the subset. Clause database in CSR form over [i64] (literals, clause offsets), two-watched-literal lists as intrusive arrays, a trail with decision levels, VSIDS activity as [f64] with a heap over arrays, conflict analysis (first UIP) producing learned clauses into a fixed-size alloc'd arena with PicoSAT-style reduce when full, Luby restarts, iterative loops with explicit stacks (no recursion), `Enum.reduce_while` over a bounded step budget as the main loop (there is no `while`; the budget is a declared limit: a solve that exceeds it returns :unknown, reported as a limit). The batch form: `solve_all(cnf :: [i64], offsets :: [i64], queries :: [i64], ...) :: {[i64], ...}` runs Crux's enumeration in one call. State: under the defk-n4r.4 rule a helper returns every array it writes (up to seven here); use one state array with fixed offsets so helpers return one array, and record how that reads.

Pre-registered sizes and expected verdicts (against an optimized Elixir solver, which must be written: a 20-line DPLL sketch exists in the research; the baseline needs unit propagation and watched literals in Elixir before it is :optimized):
- S1 one call, ~27 vars / 63 clauses (Ash-shaped): marginal (the per-call cost ~ the packing cost).
- S2 one call, ~105 vars / 270 clauses: good, provisional.
- S3 the whole Crux enumeration in one call (1,548 solves): good (Crux + Elixir DPLL 588-953 ms, Crux + picosat 101-108 ms, measured on a busy machine).
- S4 random 3-SAT n = 200 at ratio 4.26: good (picosat 25-88 ms).
- S5 responsiveness at n = 300: the tick gap per side, beside the verdict (`responsiveness:` in Defk.Bench).

Agreement: kernel vs Elixir mode exact (===) with tie-breaks and the restart/reduce schedule pinned; kernel vs the anchors: same SAT/UNSAT status and a model that satisfies every clause (check it); batch form: the scenario sets must cover the formula equivalently, not match the list (Crux's sets differed between solvers in 2 of 6 shapes tried, all valid).

Needs: defk-n4r.4 (helpers writing arrays they return; blocked by defk-auo), defk-ivt (done), defk-w38 optional; watch for code size (defk-6ag). Not needed: defk-cmr, defk-n4r.3, defk-sve.

Done when: the five sizes are measured with the pre-registered verdicts, agreement holds as defined, and the tick-gap table is recorded beside the verdict.

comments.text:
Landed on branch defk-52v.15/cdcl-sat (575e952; stages 722b5eb, 71ec97c, db623f9, 58a233f; main merged at 4a0ed70). examples/cdcl_sat.exs, README row, docs/performance.md 2.17, 5.10, 6.24, 7.9.

Verdicts (M4 Pro, load 3.5-7.7, four runs, provisional; baseline :optimized):
- S1 one solve/call, Ash P=4 (26-28 vars): pre-registered marginal, measured GOOD 2.3-5.3x (best Elixir 3.8-8.2 ms vs defk 1.5-1.6 ms per 200 calls); 1.63-1.76x vs picosat.
- S2 one solve/call, Ash P=12 (104-109 vars): good, 2.48-2.58x (near the line); 1.68-1.75x vs picosat.
- S3 whole Crux.satisfying_scenarios, P=12 (89 scenarios): good, 11.8-12.4x (217-224 vs 17.5-18.7 ms); 4.05-4.09x faster than Crux+picosat (71-73 ms).
- S4 random 3-SAT n=200 x3 seeds: good, 5.7-5.8x (1167-1198 vs 201-207 ms); 0.65x of picosat (stronger search on the UNSAT seed: 86-88 vs 170 ms).
- S5 tick gap n=300 seed 7 (max ms): picosat 1270-1342 (whole solve), defk 2.5-6.0 (p99 2.3), Elixir 2.1-3.0 (one 136 outlier); idle floor 2.0. Solve: picosat 1.27-1.30 s, defk 1.95-1.98 s, Elixir CDCL 10.8-11.3 s.

Design: one [i64] state array with header offsets (helpers return st only); integer VSIDS (not [f64]) so the Elixir baseline can keep the same algorithm in :atomics; blockers, local minimisation, Luby, LBD-bucket reduce, forced restart+reduce when the arena is full, status 2 for budget/arena limits. solve_all runs Crux's loop with Crux's negation encoding; status 3 = output capacity, retried x4.

Elixir tried: the same CDCL on one :atomics array (=== the kernel: status, model, conflicts), the DPLL sketch (used per formula where faster), Crux on the Elixir CDCL vs the loop in Elixir (12-16% faster at P=12), simple_sat. Not tried: functional CDCL, state kept across calls.

Agreement: kernel === Elixir mode (140 CNFs incl. near-threshold 3-SAT with a tiny arena; solve_all on P<=4 shapes), === Elixir CDCL (2,000 CNFs + 200 3-SAT), status = picosat and models valid (2,000), simple_sat (300), forced yields, bad literals raise; batch covers valid (sufficient + covering, checked with picosat) at all 8 shapes, sets differ from picosat's at 4 of 8.

Language: defk-tif filed (helper in one reduce_while branch copies the accumulator every iteration when another tail returns it; cost 1.9 s vs 1 ms before the restructure). Code size 2.35 MB C, 683 KB .so, ~3 min clang (every defk is its own entry point inlining its callees; defk-6ag). Our solver is weaker than PicoSAT on hard n=300 (4 of 7 seeds > 60 s).

title: Bounded CDCL SAT kernel vs picosat_elixir and simple_sat, measured on Crux's scenario enumeration
